summary.bn: আটটা LED দিয়ে একটা অঙ্ক: a থেকে g সেগমেন্ট আর দশমিক বিন্দু
summary.en: One digit made of eight LEDs: segments a to g and a decimal point

simplified: Each segment is a red LED, about 1.8 V forward, like the lab's red LED. A segment lights while current flows through it; it needs its own resistor (start with 220 Ω to 1 kΩ).

The display can be common cathode (the shared leg to GND, a segment's leg taken HIGH to light it) or common anode (the shared leg to the supply, a segment's leg taken LOW). Choose which in the inspector; a real one says which on its label or datasheet.
Its two COM legs are joined inside, as on the real display.
The legs are in the common 10-pin order: bottom row e, d, COM, c, DP from the left, top row g, f, COM, a, b. Some displays differ: read your datasheet.
It stands across the centre gap, its rows 0.6 inch apart, in rows d and h.
